selected_problem: Fresh-main inspection after v0.12.82 found that terminal dot segments still lose directory intent during path normalization. A relative require/import such as '.' can normalize to 'src' and incorrectly prefer a sibling src.js over src/index.js, while '..' from src/main can normalize to the repository root and lose the root-directory index candidate entirely.
decision_basis: The defect is determined by the resolver's already-established directory-index behavior; no parser, bundler, package-resolution or filesystem identity architecture needs to be chosen.
Terminal '.' and '..' segments are directory references, so preserving that intent is a local path-semantics invariant rather than a new product feature.
The repair keeps ordinary file-extension and extensionless inference unchanged while making current-directory and parent-directory intent explicit after normalization.
changes: normalizeImport now preserves directory intent when the source specifier ends in '/', '.' or '..', including dot segments that disappear during lexical normalization.
Repository-root directory intent is represented explicitly and index inference can resolve root index.* candidates without treating sibling files as direct targets.
tests/semantic-import-target-resolution.test.mjs adds regressions for require('.') and require('..') while retaining all prior resolver cases.
